weights_gb_note: decimal GB; bf16 = sum of safetensors sizes on the hub (equals 2 x params); 4bit = NF4 + double-quant estimate: 68.451 B quantisable linear params x 0.5159 B + remaining params in bf16
fits_single_80gb_detail: bf16: NO (141.1 GB weights); 4bit (bnb NF4 + double-quant, bf16 compute): ~39.5 GB weights, leaves ~35 GB of an 80 GB card for KV cache (0.31 MB/token) and activations. Call adapter.load(quant='4bit'); loading the bf16 repos with quant=None on less than ~148 GB of visible GPU memory raises MemoryError (a pre-quantised 4-bit repo such as unsloth/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-bnb-4bit is measured at its 4-bit size, so quant=None is fine for it). Scope: this is the weights + GENERATION budget (Ctx.gen / Ctx.run); direction building (core.Ctx.hidden_last / neutral_stats keep 81 hidden-state tensors, all-position logits and a KV cache for a whole chunk of up to 14,000 padded prompt tokens) has its own budget, see hidden_last_long_context: 61.7-66.3 GB with the 4-bit weights (43.1-43.8 GB for the longest pooled prompt alone), which fits one 80 GB card (arithmetic from the real config and tokenizer, NOT run on a GPU).

hidden_last_long_context.assumes: core.Ctx.hidden_last and Ctx.neutral_stats as of SPEC v1: one forward with output_hidden_states=True over a chunk of n prompts (left-padded to T tokens, the longest of the chunk) keeps (num_layers + 1) bf16 hidden states [n, T, hidden] and all-position logits [n, T, vocab], plus a KV cache (use_cache defaults to True; gb_kv_cache_upper_bound assumes full attention in every layer: exact for Llama, an over-estimate for Gemma's 5:1 sliding-window layers); the gb_* figures of the longest prompt are the n = 1 case; transient activations and allocator overhead are NOT counted, so the real need is higher
hidden_last_long_context.prompt_set: sbx.evals.get_pool()['hard'] (281 questions after the sbx.evals prompt-length cap MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=7500, 296 before it; sbx/dirs/sandbag.py:sandbag_hard calls ctx.hidden_last on all of them), framing E, meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct tokenizer (same vocab / merges / template as 3.3-70B)
hidden_last_long_context.verdict_rule: fits_80gb = gb_peak_upper_bound <= 0.9 * 85 (an '80 GB' A100/H100 has ~85e9 bytes; 10% headroom, the same rule as for the weights); a 'false' verdict additionally needs gb_peak_lower_bound > 0.9 * 85, i.e. it does not depend on the KV-cache term. Arithmetic from the real config and tokenizer, NOT run on a GPU

largest_chunk.basis: Ctx.hidden_last and Ctx.neutral_stats forward chunks of prompts, not single prompts: core.batches() packs the prompts, shortest first, into chunks of at most tok_budget = 14000 padded prompt tokens (prompts x the longest prompt of the chunk; only a single prompt above the budget makes a bigger chunk) and that budget does not depend on the model or on the free memory, so the memory peak is set by the biggest chunk. The figures for the longest prompt alone underestimate it whenever that prompt is shorter than the budget, which holds for every pooled prompt since the sbx.evals prompt cap. tokens = max(tok_budget, longest_prompt_tokens) is an upper bound on the padded tokens of one chunk (a smaller prefill or KV budget on a small GPU can make the real chunks smaller); the sizes are the same formulas as above at that many tokens
largest_chunk.verdict_rule: fits = gb_peak_upper_bound <= 0.9 * 85; does not fit = gb_peak_lower_bound > 0.9 * 85 (independent of the KV-cache term); borderline = in between (the lower bound is below the 90% line, the upper bound is above it). Same thresholds as fits_80gb above. Arithmetic from the real config and tokenizer, NOT run on a GPU

access_check.method: HfApi.model_info + HTTP HEAD with the local HF token on config.json and the first safetensors shard (200/302 = accessible, 403 = gated and access not granted)

min_transformers_note: llama3 rope scaling landed in 4.43.0 (Llama-3.1); only 4.57.6 was actually run here

layer_path_verified.method: AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(real hub config) under accelerate.init_empty_weights (meta device) + tie_weights(); numerics of the 1-based convention on a tiny random model of the same HF class (sbx/tests/test_adapters_gemma_llama.py)
layer_path_verified.convention: hidden_states[L] == output of layers[L-1] for 1 <= L < nl (exact); hidden_states[nl] is post final norm (avoid L = nl)
layer_path_verified.config_source: unsloth/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct config.json (weights are sha256-identical to the official repo; the official config is not accessible with the local token)

est_prompt_tokens.basis: measured mean over data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl (400 four-option questions) with the real tokenizer + adapter.build; the long-context sets are longer but bounded by the sbx.evals prompt-length cap (MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=7500): every question served by sbx.evals builds a framing-E prompt of at most 2,892 tokens (a GPQA-bio question) and the LAB-Bench sets average ~0.7k (labbench_seqqa), ~1.2k (labbench_protocolqa) and ~1.6k (labbench_cloning, 6 questions left) tokens with framing N; the raw LAB-Bench files have prompts of up to 51k characters (docs/evals.md section 3)

est_tokens_per_question_basis: ESTIMATE of generated tokens per 4-option bio MCQ under the cot prompt (prior knowledge of how verbose these models are); NOT measured (no weights available locally). Replace with the mean generated length from the first GPU run; max_new=512 truncates longer answers (they count as unparsed).
template_notes:
Chat template (3.1-8B and the official 3.3-70B tokenizer_config are the same string, sha256 e10ca381b1ccc5cf; vocab and merges identical): '<|begin_of_text|>' + ALWAYS a system header '<|start_header_id|>system<|end_header_id|>

Cutting Knowledge Date: December 2023
Today Date: {date_string}

{system}<|eot_id|>' (even with no system message), then '<|start_header_id|>user<|end_header_id|>

{user}<|eot_id|>'; generation prompt '<|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|>

'. The 3.1/3.3 template defaults the date to the fixed '26 Jul 2024' (verified); a variant defaulting to strftime_now() (I believe Llama-3.2-style templates do; not checked) would make prompts depend on the day, so render() always passes date_string='26 Jul 2024' explicitly (the tests build such a variant to prove it). Framing text goes in the system role after the date lines (sys_role='system'). BOS comes from the template; Adapter.encode uses add_special_tokens=False -> exactly one BOS. Generation stops at eos ids [128001, 128008, 128009]; decoded text ends with '<|eot_id|>' then pad tokens.
known_issues: GATED and NOT accessible with the local token (HTTP 403 GatedRepoError on config.json and on the shards, checked 2026-11-21). Either request access to meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, or load the ungated mirror unsloth/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (all 30 safetensors shards have identical size+sha256 to the official repo per the HF API; its config.json / tokenizer_config.json differ in small ways (pad token, single eos id) but chat_template, vocab and merges are identical): adapter.load(repo='unsloth/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct', quant='4bit').

Download is 141 GB of bf16 shards and the 4-bit quantisation happens at load time. A pre-quantised alternative is unsloth/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-bnb-4bit (39.5 GB, ungated; its config.json quantization_config is NF4 + double-quant + bf16 compute with embed_tokens/lm_head skipped, i.e. the same settings load(quant='4bit') builds; load it with quant=None: transformers then uses the checkpoint's own quantization_config, and adapter.load()'s GPU-memory guard reads that config.json and measures the repo at its 4-bit size (39.5 GB), not at the 141 GB of the official bf16 repo; quant='4bit' with the same repo also works: transformers 4.57.6 (quantizers/auto.py get_hf_quantizer / merge_quantization_configs; library code read, the load itself was NOT run: no bitsandbytes / CUDA locally) uses the checkpoint's own quantization_config and only warns that the one passed in is ignored (a quantization_config of a different class would raise ValueError). It is the uploader's quantisation of the same weights, so treat results as 4-bit either way.

bf16 does not fit one 80 GB GPU (141.1 GB): load(quant=None) on the bf16 repos raises MemoryError when <~148 GB of GPU memory is visible (a pre-quantised 4-bit repo is measured at its 4-bit size); use quant='4bit' (NF4 + double-quant, bf16 compute, ~39.5 GB) or 2 x 80 GB for bf16.

Hooks work with bnb-4bit layers: bitsandbytes only replaces the nn.Linear children of each LlamaDecoderLayer with Linear4bit; the decoder-layer modules and their bf16 outputs (where core.Hooks attaches) are unchanged. Established from the library code; NOT run here (no CUDA/bitsandbytes locally).
4-bit weight noise slightly perturbs all activations relative to bf16: a null result on the 4-bit model is a statement about the quantised model; cross-check against the 8B in bf16.
Tokenizer has pad '<|finetune_right_pad_id|>' in the official 3.3 tokenizer_config (3.1 has none; adapter.load() sets it for both). N prompts contain the system date header.

Long-context sets are short since the sbx.evals prompt-length cap (MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=7500): the longest served prompt has 2,892 tokens with framing E (a GPQA-bio question) and the LAB-Bench sets reach ~2.3k, but the 70B's KV cache is 0.31 MB/token (about 1.1 GB for a 2.9k-token prompt plus max_new=512), so core.batches() still builds small chunks for them; it budgets this from free memory.
Not run on real weights (none available locally): max_new, est_tokens_per_question and output formats are unmeasured; mechanics were verified on a tiny random LlamaForCausalLM.
recommended_gpu: 1 x 80 GB (A100-80GB / H100) with quant='4bit' (~39.5 GB weights) for generation; bf16 needs 2 x 80 GB (141.1 GB, ~19 GB left for KV). Hidden-state extraction (core.Ctx.hidden_last) also fits one 80 GB card with the 4-bit weights: ~43-44 GB for the longest pooled prompt (2,272 tokens) and ~62-66 GB for the largest chunk core.batches() builds (14,000 padded prompt tokens), see hidden_last_long_context (arithmetic, NOT run on a GPU; the bf16 weights were not analysed).
download_gb_note: sum of the bf16 safetensors shards (plus a few MB of tokenizer/config files); the pre-quantised alternative unsloth/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-bnb-4bit is 39.5 GB

ungated_mirror.evidence: HfApi.model_info(files_metadata=True): 30/30 safetensors shards with identical size and lfs sha256 to meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (2026-11-21)
ungated_mirror.differences: config.json adds head_dim/pad_token_id (128004)/unsloth_fixed and a single eos_token_id (128009; its generation_config.json keeps the official eos list [128001, 128008, 128009]); tokenizer_config/special_tokens_map set the pad token; the official tokenizer_config.json (byte-identical copy fetched from another public mirror) has the same chat_template, and vocab, merges and tokenizer.json are identical
